# Agent instructions for this repository

This repo holds portable AI agent configuration — skills, subagents and hooks authored once and consumed by both Claude Code and GitHub Copilot.

## The one rule that matters

**`.claude/` is the source of truth. `.github/` is generated. Never hand-edit anything under `.github/` except `workflows/`, `dependabot.yml` and `CODEOWNERS`.**

Generated files carry a `GENERATED by scripts/sync.mjs` header. If you change a skill or agent, run:

```bash
npm run sync
```

CI fails if the generated tree is stale. It never regenerates for you — it only verifies.

## Why the layout is what it is

Copilot loads agent skills from `.github/skills`, `.claude/skills` **or** `.agents/skills`. Claude Code loads them only from `.claude/skills`. So `.claude/skills/` is the single directory both tools read natively — that is why it is canonical, and why skills are the preferred unit of authorship.

Subagents and slash commands do not enjoy that overlap: Copilot reads subagents only from `.github/agents/`, and prompt files only from `.github/prompts/` (VS Code and Visual Studio only — Copilot CLI does not support prompt files at all). Those directories therefore hold generated pointer stubs containing no substance of their own.

Full compatibility matrix: [docs/portability.md](../docs/portability.md).

## Authoring

- **Prefer a skill.** If a capability can be expressed as a skill, make it one — skills are the only primitive that ports cleanly.
- Skills live at `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and follow the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification): frontmatter `name` must equal the directory name, be kebab-case and ≤64 characters; `description` is required, ≤1024 characters, and must state both *what* the skill does and *when* to use it. No angle brackets anywhere in frontmatter.
- Skill bodies must **degrade gracefully across runtimes**. Claude Code can spawn parallel subagents; Copilot CLI cannot. Write instructions that say what to do in each case rather than assuming one runtime.
- Do not create `.claude/commands/`. Claude Code already exposes skills as `/<name>`, so a command file would duplicate a skill for no gain.
- Details and worked examples: [docs/authoring.md](../docs/authoring.md).

## Security posture

This repo distributes things that execute on other people's machines. Treat it accordingly.

- Dependency budget is **two packages** — `js-yaml` and its only child `argparse`. Tests use the built-in `node:test` runner. Adding a dependency needs a justification in the PR.
- `.npmrc` sets `ignore-scripts=true`. Use `npm ci`, never `npm install`, in any automation.
- Every GitHub Action is pinned to a full commit SHA. Workflows hold no write permissions and reference no secrets.
- `.claude/hooks/` is the highest-risk surface — hooks are shell that runs automatically. Every hook change is a privileged change and `tests/hygiene.test.mjs` enforces a safety floor on them.

Full rationale: [docs/security.md](../docs/security.md).

## Before you finish

Run `/done`. It audits documentation and test coverage for the session's changes, runs validation, and opens a PR only if all gates pass.

## Conventions

- No absolute home directory paths, no employer-specific or work-internal content anywhere in the repo. `tests/hygiene.test.mjs` enforces this.
- Markdown only under `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/agents/`, `.github/agents/` and `.github/prompts/`.
- File names are lowercase kebab-case.
